title: Batch the terminal archive projection lock
summary: terminal_archive_projection previously called load_archived_snapshot() once per terminal fact, and each call independently acquired and released the shared canonical task-state flock (.orchestrator/task-state.lock). This made a single status command's archive scan take/drop the same shared lock hundreds of times as the archive grows, forcing the supervisor tick to queue behind that thrash. Commit e93e5d2c4 wraps the whole per-fact scan in one canonical_task_state_lock_file(shared=True) acquisition; because that lock is process-thread re-entrant for the same resolved path (see .orchestrator/common.py stable_sidecar_lock), every nested lock acquisition performed inside load_archived_snapshot() during the scan becomes a cheap in-process depth increment instead of a real flock(2) syscall, with identical read semantics and output.

change.description: Acquire task_archive_module.STATUS_FILE's canonical task-state shared lock once around the sorted-facts loop, referenced as a module attribute (not a name bound at import time) so test monkeypatching of task_archive.STATUS_FILE keeps resolving to the same lock path as load_archived_snapshot()'s own internal lock acquisition.

acceptance_verification.requirement: Keep terminal_archive_projection output identical: same rows and same archive_missing / archive_receipt_valid values for every terminal fact.
acceptance_verification.evidence: scripts/test_ai_status.py::ArchiveWorkflowTests::test_terminal_projection_reports_missing_archive_without_losing_fact exercises exactly these row fields (archive_missing, archive_receipt_valid) and passed unchanged at this head.

acceptance_verification.requirement: Prove the lock traffic drop with a reproducible measurement rather than an assertion: count fcntl.flock calls before and after over the same archive size.
acceptance_verification.evidence: Independently reproduced (owner re-verification of the pushed head, not re-implementation) with PANTHEON_RUNTIME_LOCK_TRACE, which appends one line per real acquire/release syscall performed by stable_sidecar_lock in .orchestrator/common.py (re-entrant depth increments emit no trace line, so the count reflects actual flock(2) calls only). Fixture: 200 synthetic terminal facts, each with a matching archived snapshot file under a temp ai-task-archive/tasks directory, calling status_projection.terminal_archive_projection(state) directly, both against the pre-fix tree (git show 4d78e49fe, the direct parent of e93e5d2c4) and against this PR's tree.

before_fix.source: git show 4d78e49fe:.orchestrator/rewrite/status_projection.py (parent of e93e5d2c4; per-fact load_archived_snapshot calls with no outer shared lock)

measurement.reduction: 200 real flock cycles -> 1 real flock cycle for a 200-terminal-fact scan (O(n) -> O(1))
measurement.note: The commit message on e93e5d2c4 additionally reports 386 flock calls before / 2 after on an isolated 193-task archive fixture, consistent with this independent re-measurement's O(n) -> O(1) shape (the 2-vs-1 acquire/release pairing is the same single lock cycle, just counted per direction).

acceptance_verification.requirement: Do not weaken or delete any existing assertion; scripts.test_ai_status must pass in full.
acceptance_verification.evidence: Full suite run at this head: .venv-pantheon/bin/python3 -m pytest -q scripts/test_ai_status.py -> '512 passed, 345 subtests passed in 275.72s (0:04:35)'. No test was modified, skipped, or removed.

acceptance_verification.requirement: Source and isolated-test scope only. No hosted deployment and no live config edit; the live supervisor config is a promotion render artifact.
acceptance_verification.evidence: Only .orchestrator/rewrite/status_projection.py is touched by the implementation commit. No config, workflow, or deployment file was changed; verification ran entirely via local pytest and a local Python reproduction script against temp directories.

no_regressions: terminal_archive_projection's row shape, sort order, and archive_missing/archive_receipt_valid computation are byte-for-byte unchanged; only the lock acquisition boundary moved from per-iteration to per-scan.
risk_notes: canonical_task_state_lock_file is documented in .orchestrator/common.py as process-thread re-entrant for an identical resolved lock path. The fix relies on that existing contract rather than introducing new locking behavior, and reads task_archive_module.STATUS_FILE dynamically (not a name captured at import time) so it keeps resolving to the same lock path as load_archived_snapshot()'s own internal call even when tests monkeypatch task_archive.STATUS_FILE.
